question: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?

options.text: Debit cards are used for online transactions, while credit cards are used for in-person purchases.
Credit cards require a PIN, while debit cards require a signature.
Debit cards withdraw money directly from a bank account, while credit cards allow borrowing up to a certain limit.
Debit cards have higher interest rates than credit cards.

solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Debit cards** allow you to spend money by drawing on funds you have already deposited at the bank.
 
• **Debit cards** usually require a PIN (Personal Identification Number) for transactions, especially at ATMs and point-of-sale terminals.
 
• **Credit cards** may require a signature for transactions, but increasingly use PINs and contactless technology.
 
• Credit cards allow you to borrow money up to a certain limit, to be repaid later along with possible interest.
 
• **Interest rates** are applicable only to credit cards if the balance is not paid in full by the due date.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Debit card** transactions are directly deducted from the user's bank account.
 
• **Credit card** users can earn rewards, cash back, or air miles which may not be available with all debit cards.
 
• **Credit scores** can be positively or negatively affected by the use of credit cards, depending on the user's spending and repayment behavior.
 
• **Fraud protection** is strong for both credit and debit cards, but credit cards may offer more comprehensive protection in case of unauthorized transactions.
 
• **Overdraft fees** are generally not applicable to credit cards, but debit card users may face them if they opt into overdraft protection services and exceed their account balance.
